title: Clear a blocked washbasin with a sink plunger
instruction: Clear the blockage so this basin drains normally, then leave the drain unobstructed.
context: Household basin maintenance requires a sealed cup and pressure transmission through the waste, including control of leakage through the overflow.
setup: A full-size 350 x 280 x 140 mm ceramic wall-hung basin rests on two 40 x 60 x 20 mm white-painted steel supports. Charge the assembled basin and waste with 1.00 L of clean water; the settled water depth is about 25 mm. A 120 mm-mouth, 160 mm-long corrugated plastic sink plunger with a rubber lip stands off-centre in the bowl. Before each trial, pre-wet the cup and restore the upright offset start with the blockage untouched; no separate water dose is added. A loose 50 mm rubber cover with a pull ring is on the left. A fixed cross grate guards the 32 mm waste throat. A wet 6 g fibre/soap mat blocks the short neck above a transparent PMMA chamber (44 mm internal / 50 mm external diameter). A transparent PMMA outlet tube (32 mm bore, 38 mm outside diameter), centred 38 mm above the table, passes above the wall of a transparent PMMA graduated tray (340 mm outside / 332 mm inside diameter, 18 mm height, 4 mm bottom). The tray waterline is below the outlet. The fixed chrome-plated tap (18 mm tube, 70 mm rise above the rim, 60 mm reach) is off. The waste grate and cover pull ring are chrome-plated metal.
scoring:
All outlet water goes into one graduated receiver. Water transferred by a tool, spilled over the basin rim, or lost through a disassembled joint never counts as drainage. A final clear-bore check uses the inspection section; a real trial can also verify continued drainage with a measured refill. Full score requires the passage to remain open, not just a transient drop in basin water level.

Score 0 if the basin, waste or pipe is broken or detached; or if more than 50 mL of the starting water reaches the table/floor rather than the receiver. These failures persist for the trial.

Otherwise score 1.0 if at least 0.90 L of the initial 1.00 L has passed through the waste into the receiver, the blockage no longer bridges the 32 mm pipe bore at the obstructed section, and the nearest point of the plunger cup or sealing-rim outline is at least 30 mm from the 52 mm waste-fitting outer rim for the final 1 s. Score 0.5 if at least 0.50 L has passed through the waste into the receiver and the bore is still open at the end, but a full-score condition is unmet. Score 0.25 if at least 0.20 L has passed through the waste into the receiver and the bore is still open at the end, but the higher thresholds are unmet. Every other outcome scores 0. The bore check is a clear passage at least 24 mm in diameter through the former obstruction. The task's score and success test use the same conditions; no mandatory hand pose, stroke count, peak pressure, particular tool grip, or seal order affects the score. The run limit is 2,400 control steps, 120 s at 20 Hz.
fidelity: GPU rigid bodies with 16 spring lip sectors, an axial bellows and a single-axis wet mat. A 240 Hz lumped water/air network applies one pressure to cup, cover and mat; actual displacement and separate cup liquid conserve volume without crediting air flow. Stiffness, friction and gas compliance are engineering assumptions. Numerical force error and ≤4.5 mL bowl-volume approximation are documented in README. Water/skin are visual meshes; fixtures are rigid and fracture is not simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps). Scripted demo: 1.0 (628 steps). Uncovered-overflow control: 0.0 (602 steps).
reset_notes: Reset the wetted 6 g mat in the 32 mm neck and empty the receiver. Restore the total 1.00 L water charge, pre-wetted upright plunger at its specified offset, and loose overflow cover. There is no separately metered cup charge. The mat remains blocked; the robot establishes the working seals. The 230 mL air-equivalent compliance is an engineering approximation, not a measured reset volume.
